title: Amortized memory lanes for continuous batching and KV headroom orchestration
creator: Ravi Patel
description: Background: Continuous batching and aggressive KV caching improve throughput but create hard-to-predict memory pressure across weights, KV, and activations. Multi-tenant workloads produce transient microbursts that either cause tail latency spikes or OOM-induced throttles. Goal: introduce an "amortized memory lanes" model — lightweight, per-tenant transient pools that smooth burst allocation and provide predictable headroom without reserving large static slabs. The lanes let the scheduler amortize short-term KV/activation spikes across a sliding window, support soft preemption, and gracefully spill low-value KV to host memory or quantized backup formats.
out_of_scope: Dedicated hardware reconfiguration, long-term weight re-sharding, runtime kernel-level attention changes (will integrate with those later but not part of this ticket).
acceptance_criteria: New amortized-lane allocator implemented in serving runtime and togglable via config flag
End-to-end tests demonstrating no regression in P50 and <5% increase in P95 for steady-state throughput workloads
Reduction in OOMs and emergency spills for bursty multi-tenant testbed by >=40% vs baseline
Dashboard panels for amortization utilization, lane eviction events, KV spill rate, and per-tenant headroom occupancy
Canaries on a single dedicated cluster with automatic rollback if OOM rate increases >10% relative to baseline
implementation_notes: Allocator model: each tenant gets a baseline lane and a borrowable amortization delta computed from an EWMA of recent burstiness (configurable window and max cap)

Preemption: implement two-phase soft preempt where long-running batches publish preemptible hint metadata; eviction prefers KV entries with low access recency and lower quality score (e.g., embeddings used <X times)
Spill path: quantify an async host-spill pipeline that stores quantized KV shards in pinned host pages with LRU tagging and background compaction
Admission control: admission layer consults amortized-lane budget before scheduling and can gate batching growth to respect headroom SLOs
Telemetry: emit new metrics: amortization_util_pct, lane_borrow_count, lane_repay_rate, kv_spill_ops, avg_eviction_latency, amortized_ewma_burstiness
risks: Incorrect EWMA parameters could over- or under-estimate burst capacity causing either wasted headroom or unexpected OOMs
Host spill path adds latency for cold KV reads — need careful QoS on fallbacks
Multi-tenant fairness corner cases when several tenants burst simultaneously; must test with adversarial traces
Complexity in scheduler increases test surface and may interact with autoscaling rules
rollout_plan: Phase A: feature behind runtime flag; unit + integration tests; internal perf microbench on staging
Phase B: small canary on one Dedicated cluster for non-critical tenants (2% traffic), monitor OOMs and amortization metrics for 48h
Phase C: expand to 20% of tenants and enable KV quantized host spill; collect latency tail metrics and KV hit rate
Phase D: full enable with dynamic tuning of EWMA window based on observed burst patterns; document operator knobs in runbook
engineering_decisions: Use EWMA window (default 60s) for burst estimate to balance responsiveness and noise suppression
Opt for soft preemption with best-effort eviction ordering rather than preempting active batches
Quantized host spill format will use 4-bit product quantization for KV shards to minimize host storage and network impact
Expose per-tenant max cap as operator-settable to support high-SLA customers
